metric_definitions.invocations: Explicit recorded skill requests: native skill-prompt events, expanded command wrappers, leading slash commands, explicit skill load requests, and recognized legacy save/commit prompt bodies. A request is not proof of successful workflow completion.
metric_definitions.skill_reads: Successful read/eval tool results identifying a skill root or SKILL.md through read metadata or a skill-file header. Count at most once per skill in each tool-result record. Includes inspection/documentation reads; not equivalent to executing a skill.
metric_definitions.invocation_sessions: Distinct parent sessions with an explicit recorded invocation. Subagent transcripts are folded into their parent session.
metric_definitions.sessions: Distinct parent sessions with either an explicit invocation or a successful skill read. Repeated reads and multiple subagents do not inflate this count.
metric_definitions.current_repository: Skill had a root SKILL.md in the current repository inventory when scanned. The shared resource directory is excluded.
metric_definitions.first_seen: Earliest observed invocation or successful read within the window, not skill installation or creation date.
metric_definitions.last_seen: Latest observed invocation or successful read within the window.

legacy_normalization.git-commit: 2 historical full Conventional Commits prompt requests

limitations: The requested six-month window begins April 3, but the available source logs begin May 31, 2026. No earlier usage can be inferred.

Invocation recognition is conservative and measures recorded explicit requests, not every natural-language request or autonomous workflow-stage execution. Automatic command handling can leave no explicit invocation event.

Successful skill reads include auditing and editing skill definitions. A positive read count alone does not establish actual execution; zero explicit invocations does not establish that a skill is unused.
The inventory covers every observed skill identifier and all 64 current repository skills, not a complete historical inventory of every installed global skill.
One malformed JSON line was skipped: a tool-result record with an invalid Unicode surrogate pair and no skill path. It is not a user or skill-prompt invocation.
